extracted.intended_audience: students learning to write mathematical proofs; mathematicians (aspiring or early-career) who wish to learn how to communicate mathematical truths via proofs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for students maturing into mathematicians on how to write proofs that establish mathematical truths and communicate understanding; emphasizes correctness, clarity, explanation, and insight. Oriented to learners learning for the first time in a serious way how to produce proofs that other mathematicians can read and appreciate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical correctness / establishes conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce clear and correct mathematical arguments that logically establish their conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs should be correct and give a logical chain of reasoning that establishes the theorem or statement as true. The goal is to 'logically establish their conclusions' so that the argument is valid and convincing to other mathematicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain why (explanatory power)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs tell us not only that a mathematical statement is true, but also why it is true, and they communicate this truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond mere verification, a good proof explains the reasons behind the result; it communicates understanding of the cause or mechanism that makes the statement true, not just a certificate of truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity / communicative transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce clear mathematical arguments that render previously opaque issues transparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity means the reader's mathematical gaze can 'penetrate completely through' the argument; proofs should be written so that confounding issues become transparent and the argument is easy to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight and elegance (Aha! moments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The best proofs give us insight into the nature of mathematical reality and lead to 'Aha!' moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for proofs that provide conceptual insight and aesthetic qualities (elegance) that let the reader grasp the result in one take; while correctness is primary, insight and elegance are desirable qualities to pursue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proof as the currency of mathematical communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate mathematical truths to other mathematicians in the currency of mathematics, which is: proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write proofs with the intended audience of other mathematicians in mind — proofs are the standard mode of communicating mathematical truth in the discipline, so adopt the conventions and rigor expected by that audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate the mathematician's reasoning process
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how a mathematician makes an argument establishing a mathematical truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exposition should illuminate the process of argumentation — not merely state results but show the reasoning, methods, and structure by which the conclusion is reached, helping learners see how mathematicians think and argue.
